sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of WHO's 2011 Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Framework for the sharing of influenza viruses and access to vaccines and other benefits. It contains the title and copyright pages and contents, and begins World Health Assembly resolution WHA64.5 of 24 May 2011, which considered the report of the Open-Ended Working Group of Member States.

sections.title: WHA 64.5 Pandemic Influenza Preparedness: sharing of influenza viruses and access to vaccine sand other benefits

summary.text: Completes resolution WHA64.5, in which the Health Assembly welcomes and adopts the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Framework and asks the Director-General to implement it and report every two years through the Executive Board.

sections.title: Principles

summary.text: Sets out the Framework's principles, in which Member States recall resolution WHA60.28 and note the continuing risk of a devastating influenza pandemic, especially for developing countries. They affirm the value of rapid virus sharing alongside fair access to vaccines and benefits, and recognize the need for technology transfer and financing that makes vaccines and medicines affordable for developing countries.

sections.title: Objective

summary.text: States the Framework's objective: to improve pandemic preparedness and response by strengthening WHO's global influenza surveillance and response system, with a fair and transparent system for sharing H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses and for access to vaccines and other benefits.

sections.extract: 2. Objective The objective of the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Framework is to improve pandemic influenza preparedness and response, and strengthen the protection against the pandemic influenza by improving and strengthening the WHO global influenza surveillance and response system (“WHO GISRS”), with the objective of a fair, transparent, equitable, efficient, effective system for, on an equal footing: (i) the

sections.title: Scope

summary.text: Defines the Framework's scope as the sharing of H5N1 and other influenza viruses with human pandemic potential and related benefits, excluding seasonal influenza and other pathogens.

sections.extract: 3. Scope 3.1 This Framework applies to the sharing of H5N1 and other influenza viruses with human pandemic potential and the sharing of benefits. 3.2 This Framework does not apply to seasonal influenza viruses or other non- influenza pathogens or biological substances that may be contained in clinical specimens shared under this Framework.

sections.title: Definitions and use of terms

summary.text: Introduces the section defining terms used in the Framework.

sections.extract: 4. Definitions and use of terms For the purpose of this Framework, the following terms have the meanings assigned to them below.

sections.title: Pandemic influenza preparedness biological materials or PIP biological materials

summary.text: Defines 'PIP biological materials' as clinical specimens, wild-type and modified isolates of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza viruses, and their extracted RNA and cDNA covering whole gene coding regions.

sections.title: Other technical terms

summary.text: Defines further technical terms used in the Framework, such as genetic sequences, reference reagents, candidate vaccine viruses and wild-type influenza viruses.

sections.extract: “Genetic sequences” means the order of nucleotides found in a molecule of DNA or RNA. They contain the genetic information that determines the biological characteristics of an organism or a virus. “Reference reagents” are biological or chemical substances or organisms and parts thereof used in diagnostic or surveillance activities. summary.text: Defines the institutions involved, such as essential regulatory laboratories, influenza vaccine, diagnostic and drug manufacturers and the laboratories that make up WHO's global influenza surveillance and response system.

sections.extract: “Essential regulatory laboratories” means influenza laboratories designated by WHO located in, or associated with, national regulatory agencies and which have a critical role at the global level for developing, regulating and standardizing human influenza vaccines. sections.title: General

summary.text: Sets out that Member States should rapidly share PIP biological materials from all cases of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza through their national laboratories with a WHO Collaborating Centre or H5 Reference Laboratory of their choice. It notes they may also share bilaterally if WHO laboratories receive the materials with priority.

sections.extract: 5.1.1 Member States, through their National Influenza Centres and Other authorized laboratories, should in a rapid, systematic and timely manner provide PIP biological materials from all cases of H5N1 and other influenza viruses with human pandemic potential, as feasible, to the WHO Collaborating Centre on Influenza or WHO H5 Reference Laboratory of the originating Member State’s choice. 5.1.2 By providing PIP

summary.text: Calls for rapid sharing of genetic sequence data on potentially pandemic influenza viruses with originating laboratories and within GISRS, and asks the Director-General to seek advice on handling such data.

summary.text: Commits the Director-General to set up an electronic system to track in real time the movement of PIP biological materials into, within and out of GISRS, and to give feedback to originating laboratories and countries.

summary.text: States that Standard Material Transfer Agreement 1 governs transfers of PIP biological materials within GISRS, and that SMTA 2 will be used for agreements with entities outside it.

sections.title: WHO Coordination of pandemic influenza preparedness and response

summary.text: States that WHO will coordinate pandemic preparedness and response under the International Health Regulations (2005), with attention to fair and transparent allocation of scarce vaccines, antivirals and diagnostics according to public health risk and need.

sections.extract: WHO will coordinate influenza pandemic preparedness and response in accordance with applicable International Health Regulations (2005) provisions and this 16 Framework. summary.text: Urges Member States with advanced capacity to help others, especially developing countries, build laboratory and influenza surveillance capacity, including virus detection and research.

summary.text: Commits the Director-General to establish a WHO stockpile of vaccines for H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses, initially 150 million doses, with related equipment. It covers allocation according to expert guidance and plans for deploying the vaccines to affected countries.

summary.text: Urges manufacturers to reserve part of each production cycle of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic vaccines for developing countries and seeks timely access for them at tiered prices.

summary.text: Urges vaccine and antiviral manufacturers to apply tiered pricing that takes account of country income levels, with attention to the least developed countries.

sections.extract: As a measure to improve the affordability for developing countries of pandemic influenza vaccines and vaccines for H5N1 and other influenza viruses with human pandemic potential, and antivirals, Member States should urge influenza vaccine and antiviral manufacturers individually to implement tiered pricing for these vaccines and antivirals. summary.text: Commits WHO to continue the Global Pandemic Influenza Action Plan to Increase Vaccine Supply, including new production facilities and transfer of technology and know-how. It urges manufacturers to support technology transfer and suggests countries consider seasonal influenza vaccination to sustain local production.

sections.title: General

summary.text: Sets out that the World Health Assembly oversees the Framework with advice from the Director-General, through an oversight mechanism that includes an independent Advisory Group of international experts.

summary.text: Describes the Advisory Group's role in monitoring and advising on the Framework without administrative or public functions, its membership and reporting, and asks for a report to the Health Assembly in 2012 on its future mandate.

sections.title: Annexes

summary.text: Contains the Framework's annexes, beginning with Standard Material Transfer Agreement 1, which sets the terms for transferring PIP biological materials within GISRS. It then gives Standard Material Transfer Agreement 2 for transfers to recipients outside GISRS, including manufacturers' commitments to benefit sharing. The articles cover the parties, obligations, intellectual property, liability and dispute settlement, with signature blocks.

sections.title: Terms of reference related to work with pandemic influenza preparedness biological materials

summary.text: Annex 5 sets out the terms of reference for work with PIP biological materials by the four types of GISRS institutions: National Influenza Centres, WHO Collaborating Centres, H5 Reference Laboratories and essential regulatory laboratories. For each it describes functions such as collecting and sharing specimens and viruses, characterizing them, developing candidate vaccine viruses and reference reagents, and supporting risk assessment. It also covers biosafety, publication and recognition of originating laboratories. The annex ends with the ISBN and WHO contact details.
